title: Full-domain (q = N) security of plain swap-or-not via the generic eight-block Fourier lift
summary: The coset-cap-to-Fourier transfer (Thm l:main with Lemmas l:trim and l:plancherel) is Lean-proved for any law on S_N. Swap-or-not supplies all three inputs it needs: HMR Thm 3 for any designated (1-1/b)N set, sign mean exactly 0, and i.i.d. rounds. This gives the first fixed-round-count proof that plain swap-or-not is secure against all N adaptive two-sided queries, at about 9.0k/16.2k rounds for N=2^64 and eps=2^-32/2^-64. That is about 3x fewer than mix-and-cut but about 7-11x more than Sometimes-Recurse's expected cost, and it is worse than mix-and-cut at N=2^20.
beneficiaries: Small-domain/format-preserving-encryption theory: Hoang, Morris, Rogaway, Tessaro, Ristenpart. Also designers who need a constant-time, fully secure PRP on a small domain with a citable proof.
first_step: Write a 2-3 page corollary: TV(SN^{pr}) <= 1/2[p*delta + sqrt((p*delta)^2 + delta^{2p} + (b C_u)^p Z_{p(1-(u+2)/b)-1}(N))] with delta = b*HMR(N, N - N/b, r). Certify C_u with a rigorous tail bound. Reproduce the round table from scratch_shufflecrypto/bounds.py, then send it to the swap-or-not and SR authors for review.
measurement: An independently checked note and table. Success means a reviewer confirms the corollary and the round counts (e.g. 16,160 rounds at N=2^64, eps=2^-64) within a few percent.
risks: The composition is my own and unreviewed. C_u is currently numerical (sup over m<=45). HMR Thm 3 is peer-reviewed but not formalized. The cost of 10^4 rounds means essentially no deployment demand. SR already gives full security at about 1/10 the expected cost, and its variable time is argued harmless.

title: Updated Thorp-cipher parameter sheet: explicit partial-domain (q<=(1-a)N) and full-domain bounds
summary: Lemma noise:halves in the conditional-information companion is explicit for every d and uniform over specified lists. It lifts MRS'09's Thorp ceiling of q < N/(4 lg N) to q <= (1-a)N in O(lg N / a) rounds. At N=2^64 and eps=2^-64 it gives CCA at q=N/2 in 3,580 rounds (716 AES calls with MRS 5x batching). Combined with the lift, it gives full domain in 37k rounds (7.4k AES calls), the cheapest fixed-time full-security option in AES calls for N >= 2^32.

targets.name: Conditional information, Lemma noise:halves and Prop noise:uniform-marginals

beneficiaries: Anyone who cites MRS'09 Thorp bounds, and researchers comparing oblivious small-domain ciphers.
first_step: Check that the half-density lemma also holds for the inverse (reverse-coordinate) shuffle, which the MRS nCPA->CCA step needs. Then publish the table together with opportunity 1.
measurement: Reviewer-checked table of rounds and AES calls against MRS'09, HMR'12, MaC and SR at N = 2^20, 2^32, 2^64.
risks: The inverse-direction lemma is unchecked. Thorp only covers N = 2^d natively; decimal domains need cycle-walking, which brings back variable time. The 5x AES batching requires 32 | N. There is no deployment demand.

title: Make the spectral exponent p* (Compatibility-entropy / Random-subspace companions) effective
summary: The spectral companions prove a bounded regular moment Z_N(p*) <= 1+1/16, so each extra sweep cuts TV by a factor of about N^{-c} with no round-independent floor. That is the right shape for a cipher. However, p*, P, L and C_0 are existential: 'sufficiently large' thresholds plus a compactness base case from Lemma lem:finitegap. An effective p* of about 10 or less would make fixed-time Thorp competitive with SR.

targets.name: Compatibility entropy Thm tra:duality:moment and Cor cor:intro-consequences
Random-subspace Thm ten:lowplanes:main (1/2 N^-5, P absolute)

first_step: Trace every 'sufficiently large' threshold in the Random-subspace proof (proof.tex) and see whether the base-case gap for n < n_0 can be replaced by an explicit recursion.
measurement: An explicit numeric P with the TV <= 1/2 N^-5 conclusion holding for all d.
risks: Base cases need n! state spaces, so the compactness step may not be effectivizable. The constants may come out galactic anyway.

title: Change Ethereum SHUFFLE_ROUND_COUNT (90) on the basis of the new results
summary: Ethereum's compute_shuffled_index is public-seed swap-or-not (no key), and the notion that matters is statistical near-uniformity plus limited RANDAO grinding. No full-permutation bound covers 90 rounds before or after family 238. The lift would need about 14k rounds at N ~ 2^20, while HMR already gives TV <= 2^-21.5 for any committee-sized set at 90 rounds. Exact small-N computations suggest true mixing takes only a few lg N rounds.
first_step: None. Optionally, a one-line note to eth2book that HMR's bound is vacuous for q >= N/2 at 90 rounds and that only the support bound (~2 lg N) is known for the full permutation.
risks: A change would require a hard fork, and the provable version costs about 150x for no practical gain.

title: Replace FF1 (or revive FF3-1) with Thorp/swap-or-not in FPE libraries, tokenization products or NIST SP 800-38G
summary: Deployed FPE is FF1: 10 Feistel rounds and about 10-30 AES calls, as in str4d/fpe, capitalone/fpe and Google SDP's FFX. NIST's 2025 Rev.1 draft handles small-domain attacks with a 10^6 domain floor and removed FF3/FF3-1. Provable full-domain Thorp or swap-or-not costs 10^3-10^4 AES calls, a 100-1000x slowdown, so nothing in these libraries or standards changes.

targets.name: str4d/fpe FF1 domain floor and 10-round loop

first_step: None. Unrelated side observation: capitalone/fpe defaults to feistelMin = 100, below the Rev.1 requirement of 10^6.

title: Use the paper's literal 1600d / 512d / 1/2 N^-5 statements as cipher round counts
summary: The 1600d bound has a round-independent floor of 8.6e7 N^{-3/2}: 2^-3.6 at 2^20, 2^-21.6 at 2^32, 2^-69.6 at 2^64. The Lean-certified fullRate is cruder and vacuous at 2^20. 512d is asymptotic with floor 18.6 N^{-1/8}. The N^-5 and spectral results have non-explicit sweep counts. None is a usable parameter; the optimized lift (rows 1-2) is the only explicit route.

title: Iterated Thorp/butterfly networks for oblivious shuffles (MPC, ORAM, mixnets) or physical card shuffling
summary: Production oblivious shuffles route a sampled permutation through a Benes/Waksman network, which is exact at depth 2 lg N - 1, or use sorting networks. Iterated Thorp layers need 1600 lg N layers, or about 10^4 by the optimized bound, and each layer costs a communication round in MPC. Card-game software uses PRNG plus Fisher-Yates.
